threads.body: [General] Because `emitSpan` is invoked only from `OnMethodExit`, starting and ending here makes every parsing-error SERVER span—and its `http.server.request.duration` metric—measure essentially zero time, excluding even a custom parsing handler's response-generation work. Start the instrumenter on method entry and carry its context to method exit, where the response is available for `end`.

[General] This new SERVER-span path bypasses `HttpServerResponseCustomizerHolder`, whereas the regular Pekko path runs it before ending the span (`PekkoHttpServerSingletons.java:42-60`). As a result, agent extensions that append response headers from the server span context do not run for parsing-error responses. Run the customizer with `PekkoHttpResponseMutator`, return the possibly header-enriched immutable response, and replace the advice return value with it.

[General] Because this type matcher intentionally includes user-defined subclasses, matching only the method name and arity also advises any unrelated four-argument `handle` overload on a custom handler. Such an overload will start a bogus SERVER span and can leave it unended when its return value cannot be cast to `HttpResponse`. Match the four parameter types from `ParsingErrorHandler.handle` explicitly.

[Security] The rejected target is decoded verbatim into default `url.path`/`url.query` attributes. Pekko permits bytes such as NUL and ESC in the token before rejecting it, so unauthenticated input can inject control characters into logging exporters and downstream telemetry. Encode or strip control bytes before exposing this raw target, or omit these URL attributes when validation failed.

replies.body:
The control characters this names were already encoded when the comment was written, the diff it is against is 6096b416a9 and 93701fdb3d added `escapeControlCharacters` after it. It runs in the private constructor, so both a target pekko-http parsed and one that failed to parse go through it, NUL and ESC included.

Checking it did turn up a real gap next door though, so thank you for it. The raw target is decoded with `utf8String()`, which turns two bytes on the wire into one C1 character, and those were left alone. `0xC2 0x9B` arrives as U+009B and went into `url.path` as it was. Fixed in 6e0252adfe, the range is now `0x00-0x1f` and `0x7f-0x9f`, with a test that sends the bytes rather than the character.

The negative control for it is worth a look, because reverting the one condition gives you this:

```
expected: "/bad%1Bpath%9B"
 but was: "/bad%1Bpath"
```

Those look like they differ by a suffix. They do not, the raw U+009B is in the actual value and renders as nothing, which is the whole problem.

On the other half of the suggestion, omitting the URL attributes when validation failed: I have deliberately not done that. The rejected target is the only description these spans have, they exist precisely because the request never became an `HttpRequest`, so dropping it leaves a span that says almost nothing. Encoding keeps it readable and safe. Happy to switch to omitting if you would rather take the stricter line.

threads.body: [General] This advice does not cover every parsing failure: on EOF while a request line/header is incomplete, `HttpMessageParser.shouldComplete()` emits `CompletionIsMessageStartError` directly without calling `failMessageStart`. The handler then receives an unbound `ErrorInfo`, so a method and target already captured from a complete request line are dropped. Bind request data when any `MessageStartError` is emitted and add a truncated-request regression test.

[Naming] A `static final VirtualField` is a semantic handle and must use `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`; rename `parserRequestLine` to `PARSER_REQUEST_LINE` and update its references.

This issue also appears on line 48 of the same file.

[General] `uriBytes` can still belong to the previous keep-alive request on this branch. Pekko throws `UriTooLong` from `findUriEnd()` before assigning `uriBytes`, so an overlong second target is reported as the first request's path. Clear the actual parser field when a new message starts (and cover this case in the carry-over test) before reading it on exceptional exit.

[General] Failed non-origin-form targets can put the full request target in `url.path`. Only emit `url.path` when the raw target starts with `/`; otherwise omit it because the path component cannot be recovered safely.

replies.body:
Done in 2d48b6229c. Only a target that starts with `/` becomes `url.path` now; an absolute form one, an authority form one, or one too broken to tell the two apart is left out rather than cut into a path it is not.

The check is in the unparsed branch only. A request line that pekko-http did parse already gives `uri.path()`, which is a path whatever form the target arrived in, so nothing changes there.

`absoluteFormTargetIsNotReportedAsAPath` covers it and it is load bearing: with the condition taken back out it fails with the whole of `http://example.com/bad%%` sitting in `url.path`.

replies.body:
Good catch, done in 2d48b6229c.

There is a `PekkoHttpRequestLine` now that just holds the `HttpMethod`, the `Uri` and the `ByteString` the parser already has. Rendering the target and scanning it for characters that need encoding moved into `toParsingError`, which is called from `bindRequestLine` and so only runs for a `MessageStartError`. threads.body: [General] These parsing-error spans omit the peer address even though the parser's stream `Attributes` already contain `PekkoHttpServerRemoteAddress`. Carry that value into this state and expose it through `getNetworkPeerInetSocketAddress`, as the existing HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 paths do.

replies.body:
Done in 2d48b6229c, and it needed less machinery than I expected.

`GraphStageLogic.attributes()` is public, and `PhasedFusingActorMaterializer` assigns it the combined inherited attributes at materialization time. The parser logic is itself the `GraphStageLogic`, so it already carries the attributes that `HttpPrepareAttributesInstrumentation` put `PekkoHttpServerRemoteAddress` on. No extra instrumentation was needed, the lookup happens on the parser that `bindRequestLine` already holds.

The tests pin the exact client port rather than just asserting an address is present, so they show it is that connection's peer and not merely some address: `client.address`, `network.peer.address` and `network.peer.port` all match the socket the request went out on.

One gap left deliberately: a rejection that no parser produced (the CONNECT case in the other thread) has no parser to take the address from, so those spans still have no peer.

threads.body: [General] An unbound `ErrorInfo` does not prove a parser rejection. `ControllerStage` also calls this handler for response and entity-stream failures after the normal server span ends, so this fallback creates a second SERVER span. Mark every pre-request rejection explicitly and skip unmarked calls.

replies.body:
This one is real and it was the significant find, thank you. Fixed in 2d48b6229c.

`finishWithIllegalRequestError` has four call sites in `ControllerStage`, not one. Line 467 is the `MessageStartError` grab, but 539, 549 and 552 (`EntityStreamException`, `EntityStreamSizeException`, `IllegalUriException`) are all in `httpResponseIn`'s `onUpstreamFailure`, which is after the request has been delivered and already has a span of its own. The `UNKNOWN` fallback turned each of those into a bogus second SERVER span.

Marking in the parser turned out not to be enough, which is worth spelling out because it is not obvious. `establishAbsoluteUri` in `HttpServerBluePrint.parsing` builds `MessageStartError`s of its own for a CONNECT request and for a `Host` header that will not resolve, and neither passes through a parser, so marking only in the parser would have silently stopped tracing those. The mark therefore goes on building the `MessageStartError`, which is exactly where the two part company: a rejection of an undelivered request is carried in one, the failures that follow a delivered request never are.

On the test, straight up: I could not get a regression test to reach those three call sites. I wrote one driving a request entity stream failure through a handler that reads the entity, and it passed with the fix reverted; a second attempt using a small `max-content-length` with a chunked entity did too. Neither actually reached `finishWithIllegalRequestError`, so rather than leave a test that passes with and without the fix I dropped it.

What is covered instead is `connectRequestIsTraced`, which is load bearing for the marking: unregister `MessageStartErrorInstrumentation` and it fails with `Error waiting for 1 traces` while the other seven still pass. So the three post-delivery call sites are justified by reading the blueprint rather than by a regression test. If you have a reproduction for the entity stream route I will happily add it.

threads.body:
A narrower implementation could keep only:

- `MessageStartErrorInstrumentation`, to mark failures that happen before request delivery
- `ParsingErrorHandlerInstrumentation`, to cover handler execution and capture the response

That would still fix the original problem by producing a SERVER span with the response status, duration, response-header capture, and response customization. The tradeoff is that these spans would be intentionally sparse: the span name would be `HTTP`, `http.request.method` would be `_OTHER`, and URL and peer attributes would be absent.

By AI rough line count guess, this could reduce production code from about 806 added lines to about 385, and tests from 524 lines to roughly 160-200. It would remove around 55-60% of the total change and avoid depending on Pekko's private parser fields and `emit$` bytecode shape across the open-ended `[1.0,)` support range.

The current richer implementation could be justified if method, target, and peer details on rejected requests are important. If the main goal is simply to stop dropping these requests from traces, the two-hook version may be a worthwhile option until Pekko exposes the rejected request context directly through apache/pekko-http#1245.

Done in a15f6a2610 with `unknownMethodIsTraced` in `PekkoHttpServerParsingErrorTest`. It sends `TEST /success` over a raw socket, checks the `501 Not Implemented` status line, and asserts the span exactly: name `HTTP`, kind SERVER, error status, and only `http.response.status_code=501` and `error.type="501"`.
